claims.text: YBa2Cu3O7–δ (YBCO) is a cuprate material with superconducting properties.
Optimizing the oxygen content of YBCO improves its superconducting properties.
Optimized oxygen content creates highly ordered CuO2 planes.
The CuO2 planes in YBCO are responsible for electron pairing.
Non-optimized oxygen stoichiometry produces disordered oxygen vacancies in YBCO.
Non-optimized oxygen stoichiometry leads to suboptimal formation of conductive CuO2 planes.
Annealing YBCO in an oxygen-rich environment can tune its oxygen stoichiometry.
Changing oxygen partial pressure and annealing temperature adjusts the oxygen content of YBCO.
Oxygen optimization promotes ordering in the CuO2 planes and alignment of the oxygen sublattice in the perovskite structure.
Proper oxygen ordering enhances carrier concentration in the CuO2 planes.
Proper oxygen ordering enhances electronic bandwidth in the CuO2 planes.
Enhanced carrier concentration and electronic bandwidth strengthen the electron-pairing interactions that produce superconductivity.
Optimized oxygen content will produce a sharper resistive superconducting transition than non-optimal oxygen content.
Optimized oxygen content will produce a higher superconducting transition temperature than non-optimal oxygen content.
YBCO prepared without controlled oxygen optimization typically has a broader superconducting transition and lower Tc because of oxygen-vacancy disorder.
The proposed oxygen-ordering effect is specific to cuprate superconductors in which CuO2-plane structure governs superconductivity.
The proposed effect may not apply to metallic or iron-based superconductors.
